messages.subject: problems plotting
parts:
Hello happy people,

I'm fairly new to R and even newer to ggplot, so bare with me for a second. I've been trying to produce two graphs. First one is from my own data from a BeeCounter (which counts bees entering and exiting the hive). I would like to produce a histogram of 96 values plotted against an interval of 15 minutes. Here is a copy paste with the error at the bottom:

> head(cebelice)
   time c2
1 00:00  0
2 00:15  0
3 00:30  0
4 00:45  0
5 01:00  0
6 01:15  0
> dim(cebelice)
[1] 96  2
> ggplot(cebelice, aes(x=time, y=c2)) + geom_histogram()
Error in all.vars(as.formula(.$facets)) :
  could not find function "as.formula"

Is there something I'm missing?

Also, I'm trying to reproduce the wonderful barplot from Learning R (link). I basically get the same error message, even though I got a different one a few hours ago (see comments at the bottom of the page). I've been only playing with my data ("cebelice") inbetween and can't comprehend what might have gone wrong/different.

Any suggestions most welcome!

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: problems plotting
parts:
> Coupled with your successful plotting I'm strongly inclined to believe that
> this is ggplot2/R/platform problem and not my data.

Then tell us some information about your R install - the output of
sessionInfo() would be a good start. The most likely explanation for
your problems is that you are using an older version of ggplot2.

Also note that R is currently reading in your time column as a factor,
which is probably not what you want, and that you're not drawing a
histogram with the data in the usual form that geom_histogram expects.
As in learnr's final example, you probably want to use geom_bar(stat
= "identity").

Hadley

--
http://had.co.nz/

> Thank you for taking interest in my problem. Here is the output of my
> sessionInfo(). Additionally, I'm using Win XP if that's of any help.

Nothing looks obviously wrong there. Have you tried running the code
in a clean session?

> Myself being a novice in these waters, could you direct me to a general
> direction in what needs to be done with my time column? Had I ventured a
> guess that I need to assign it as an as.character (since it's only a label),
> would my attempt be any more fruitful?

You need to convert it to a time. Unfortunately, that's not terribly
easy, but something like: strptime(as.character(cebelice$time),
"%H:%M") should do the job.
